about.what: The installation: table, paper, where the six arms hang, the steel around them, and the clearances every plan must keep.
about.units: metres and radians everywhere; every key that holds a length ends in _m, every angle in _rad or _deg
about.table_frame: origin at the table centre on the paper surface; x across the table (short side), y along it (long side), z up
about.old_frame: the old code (aris_sixarm) puts the origin at a canvas corner: table = old - (0.9017, 1.81532, 0). 1.81532 is half the old canvas length 3.63064.

canvas.source: old layout.SHEET_FINAL6 = (1.8034, 3.63064), centred on the table. The task sheet rounds the length to 3.6306.

arms.source: axis positions: scripts/draw_axes_frame.py, x = +-0.305 exactly; y = the old model's rows at 1/6, 1/2 and 5/6 of the 3.63064 canvas, i.e. +-1.2102133 (the drawing rounds to 1210.2 mm). Height: underside of the mounting plate 0.970 above the paper (old rig at h = 0.970). Orientation: the old model hangs every arm with R = Ry(180 deg), yaw 0, so the arm's base +x points to table -x and its base z points down. Park configurations: old aris_sixarm/layout.py Q_PARK_PROPOSED (re-derived 2026-09-10 at h = 0.970 and, for arm 31, 2026-09-14 against the seam bars, at the lateral holder tool).
arms.strut_wide_side_note: Pete measured 0.240 from the outside face of one hanging strut to the arm's axis and 0.156 to the outside face of the other. Which side the 0.240 is on is NOT confirmed. "-x" means the 0.240 side is toward table -x, "+x" toward table +x.

rows_and_phases.source: docs/DESIGN.md section 3 (Pete, 2026-09-29): three rows of two arms; phase 1 leaders 13, 71, 2; phase 2 leaders 17, 31, 97
rows_and_phases.walls_note: a wall only between leaders that can reach each other (the diagonal pairs, 1.355 apart); the two end leaders of a column are 2.42 apart and cannot

hanger.source: the steel each arm hangs from, placed relative to its own axis. Struts: Pete's tape 2026-09-16 (scripts/draw_axes_frame.py), 3 x 6 in section with the long side along y, centred on the arm's row line. Strut heights, plate and clamp: old aris_sixarm/system_model.py (drawing entities down_boom, down_plate, down_clamps; z ladder at h = 0.970).
hanger.strut_source: section and x positions: Pete's tape 2026-09-16. Bottom: the old model (system_model POST_OVER) has the posts end 34.98 mm below the plate underside; nobody will measure it, so on Pete's instruction (2026-09-30) every strut is made 0.030 longer to be conservative: 64.98 mm below the plate underside (0.970 - 0.06498). Top: old system_model GRID_U, the runway underside 1.62362.
hanger.plate_source: size: old system_model PLATE (drawing down_plate 225.82 x 190 x 12.7 mm); its underside is the mount plane. Placed centred in the slot between Pete's struts (slot 0.2436 wide, 8.9 mm free each side), which puts its centre 0.042 toward the wide side. The old model put it 25.15 mm toward table +x, which does not fit between Pete's struts.
hanger.clamp_source: old system_model CLAMP (drawing down_clamps 226 x 152.4 x 95.7 mm), sitting on the plate, same centre as the plate. Envelope only; no part number in the drawing.
hanger.own_hardware_note: an arm's own struts, plate and clamp are obstacles for it like any other steel. Its base (the kernel's link0 capsules, marked fixed) sits among them and is not checked against obstacles, because it cannot move.

steel.source: the cage, in the table frame, as axis-aligned boxes (lo_m and hi_m corners). From old aris_sixarm/system_model.py cage_bodies() and mounts.SEAM_BARS_MM, shifted into the table frame. Gussets are left out: they are ASSUMED in the old model, placed on the old post positions, and sit 1.50 m and more above the paper.

reach.source: how far any part of an arm's body can be from its shoulder, fully stretched. Bound: shoulder -> elbow 0.3266, elbow -> wrist 0.3928, wrist -> flange 0.1385 (FR3 DH), plus 0.25 for the hand, holder and pen, plus 0.08 for the fattest capsule radius = 1.188, rounded up. tests/test_rig.py checks it against the old capsule model on random configurations and against kernel.arm when present.

clearances.source: the old gates (docs/STAGED_LESSONS_2026-09-29.md L135); they do not change. The checker demands these.
clearances.wall_note: half of arm_to_arm: two arms on opposite sides of a wall are then arm_to_arm apart
clearances.tool_to_paper_note: Chosen by Pete, 2026-09-30: the tool (gripper, blades, pen holder) must not touch the paper, and nothing more. There will be no measured holder height; we work with the CAD and pen models as they are. It is also the limit on how far a pen may wear.
clearances.link1_to_own_mount_note: link 1 against the arm's OWN hanger steel (struts, plate, clamp). Link 1 and that steel are bolted to the same plate, so the 0.050 steel gate, which pays for not knowing where separate parts stand relative to each other, does not apply between them; the self clearance does. Link 1 turns about the base axis only, so this is checked once by the rig (tests/test_rig.py) and not by the collision check. Orchestrator, 2026-09-30.

planning_allowance.source: added on top of the demanded clearances when a planner asks (for_planning=True), so that the checker is a second opinion and not a coin toss (lesson L32). Set by the orchestrator 2026-09-29. The old numbers (0.013 on steel) paid for the old checker's sampling error: 0.010 half-step along a capsule plus 0.00275 between samples. The new distances are exact and both planner and checker bound the motion between samples to better than 0.001, so 0.003 covers the difference between the two with room to spare. The demanded clearances above are unchanged.
planning_allowance.arm_to_arm_note: a parked arm is as still as the steel, so it gets the steel allowance
planning_allowance.wall_note: half of arm_to_arm, because both arms at a wall pay it
planning_allowance.paper_note: zero: a pen that hovers a few millimetres over the paper before touching down cannot pay more
